tickets.title: V3.9.2 Memory Clarity: run first canon synthesis workflow
tickets.description: Execute and document the first safe canon synthesis workflow. Keep the workflow manual-first: dry-run, inspect source packet, validate generated layers, then write only when validation passes.
acceptance: Operator steps are documented for --show-packet, dry-run synthesis, validation review, and --write
Canon write path is verified to archive old canon rows and insert the expected canon layers
Validation failure remains non-destructive and reports clear errors
Docs identify canon as below filesystem/project_state but above hybrid retrieval
Regression tests covering canon validation still pass

tickets.title: V3.9.2 Memory Clarity: expose retrieval explanation details
tickets.description: Add an inspectable explanation surface for retrieved memory so Crowley can show why a memory was selected without making normal chat rigid.
acceptance: Retrieval API/debug output includes source, memory_type, score, status, pinned flag, canon flag, and available provenance ids
Prompt/retrieval explanation is read-only and does not alter ranking behavior unless explicitly needed
Keyword-only fallback still reports useful explanation fields
Tests cover explanation payload shape for vector+keyword and keyword fallback where practical

tickets.title: V3.9.2 Memory Clarity: clarify memory hierarchy language
tickets.description: Make the memory truth hierarchy easy to understand in docs and UI copy: filesystem/project_state, tickets, agent activity, canon, retrieval, recent chat.
acceptance: PRE_V4_RELEASE_PLAN, WHERE_WE_ARE, ROADMAP, and relevant memory docs describe the hierarchy consistently
Memory UI labels distinguish canon/pinned memories from ordinary retrieved memories
No copy implies canon overrides filesystem truth, project_state, or tickets
Docs preserve the rule that Crowley should be natural in conversation but auditable on demand

tickets.title: V3.9.2 Memory Clarity: add non-destructive memory hygiene checks
tickets.description: Add a dry-run hygiene path that identifies stale, noisy, duplicate, or conflicting memory rows without auto-deleting or auto-archiving anything.
acceptance: Hygiene command/API reports candidates grouped by stale, noisy, duplicate, and possible conflict
Report includes memory id, source, type, status, and short reason
No rows are changed unless an explicit existing safe path is invoked
Tests cover dry-run behavior and confirm it is non-destructive

tickets.title: V3.9.2 Memory Clarity: isolate tests from working crowley.db
tickets.description: Fix test database isolation so regression tests and probes do not pollute the real working Crowley database.
acceptance: Unit tests use an isolated temporary database or explicit test database path
Running the full suite does not add probe rows to crowley.db
Existing tests pass with the isolated database setup
Docs or test helpers make the isolation convention clear for future tests

tickets.title: V3.9.3 Planning Workflow: document planning roles and Cursor-ready tickets
tickets.description: Create a concise Planning Workflow doc that explains how Mr. Go, Codex, Cursor, and Crowley collaborate through planning packets, tickets, and handoffs.
acceptance: Doc explains roles: Mr. Go sets intent, Codex plans, Cursor builds, Crowley stores truth
Doc explains when to keep brainstorming versus when to mint tickets
Doc defines Cursor-ready tickets with scope, acceptance criteria, QA expectation, and non-goals
WHERE_WE_ARE links to the workflow doc in the agent ritual section
No wording implies direct Codex-to-Cursor messaging

tickets.title: V3.9.3 Planning Workflow: add planning packet template
tickets.description: Add a reusable planning packet template for Codex-authored initiatives before ticket minting.
acceptance: Template includes objective, context, decisions, non-goals, risks, ticket slices, acceptance criteria, QA expectations, and next action
Template can be copied into a ticket JSON packet without losing core fields
Example packet uses the Pre-V4 release plan as a realistic reference
Docs explain that planning packet approval happens before Cursor implementation

tickets.title: V3.9.3 Planning Workflow: validate ticket packets before creation
tickets.description: Improve codex_sync.py --create-tickets so invalid ticket JSON fails before partial ticket creation.
acceptance: Validation catches missing title, assignee, priority, description, and acceptance criteria
Validation reports all discovered errors in human-readable form
No tickets are created when validation fails
Existing valid ticket packet behavior remains backward compatible
Tests cover valid packet, missing fields, invalid priority, and no partial creation

tickets.title: V3.9.3 Planning Workflow: support parent initiative tickets
tickets.description: Use the existing parent_id field so release initiatives can group child Cursor tickets without schema churn.
acceptance: Ticket creation supports optional parent_id through API and sync script paths
Ticket list/sync output can show child tickets grouped under a parent initiative
UI indicates parent/child relationship without visual clutter
Tests cover parent-child create/list behavior
No migration is required beyond the existing parent_id column

tickets.title: V3.9.3 Planning Workflow: add draft ticket cleanup path
tickets.description: Add a safe way to mark draft, accidental, or superseded tickets as cancelled/replaced so Cursor does not pick up stale planning work.
acceptance: Sync/API path can mark tickets cancelled with a comment
Cancelled tickets remain queryable in history but are excluded from open work summaries
Ticket event records who cancelled and why
Docs explain when to cancel versus edit a ticket
Tests cover cancellation and open summary exclusion

tickets.title: V3.9.4 Agent Visibility: add Agent Feed tab
tickets.description: Add a dedicated Intelligence drawer tab showing recent Codex, Cursor, and Crowley agent activity from existing agent activity APIs/snapshot.
acceptance: Intelligence drawer includes an Agent Feed tab next to Tickets, Tasks, Loops, Decisions, and Memory
Tab renders recent agent events newest-first with source, timestamp, summary, and next action when available
Empty, loading, and error states match the existing drawer style
Uses existing read APIs or the existing dashboard snapshot
No direct agent-to-agent channel is introduced

tickets.title: V3.9.4 Agent Visibility: add ticket detail view
tickets.description: Make the Tickets tab useful as a live work board by exposing full ticket detail and recent ticket events.
acceptance: Selecting a ticket reveals description, acceptance criteria, status, assignee, priority, and created/updated timestamps
Ticket event history is visible for create, claim, status changes, comments, done, and linked handoff activity
Open, in-progress, blocked, done, cancelled states are visually distinct
UI remains usable on mobile and desktop widths
No destructive ticket actions are added in this ticket

tickets.title: V3.9.4 Agent Visibility: link handoffs to ticket history
tickets.description: Surface handoff-linked ticket history so Cursor's shipped work is visible from the board.
acceptance: When a ticket is closed via cursor_sync --after --ticket, the linked handoff memory id is visible in ticket detail or event history
Ticket event payload identifies the actor and linked memory where available
Agent activity and ticket history remain separate but cross-reference each other
Tests cover linked_memory_id display data in ticket event/detail API

tickets.title: V3.9.4 Agent Visibility: clarify tickets vs tasks vs open loops
tickets.description: Clarify the relationship between tickets, legacy tasks, and open loops across docs and UI language. Tickets remain the agent work board.
acceptance: Docs define tickets as agent work, tasks as lightweight todos, and open_loops as unresolved project questions/risks
UI panel labels or helper copy avoid implying tasks/open_loops are the Cursor board
Prompt/onboarding docs preserve tickets as authoritative for assigned work
No data migration is required in this ticket

tickets.title: V3.9.4 Agent Visibility: lock docs for V4 readiness
tickets.description: Update roadmap/onboarding/version docs after V3.9.2-V3.9.4 so V4 begins from a clean, current state.
acceptance: ROADMAP, WHERE_WE_ARE, PROJECT_STATE, TICKETS, and VERSIONS reflect the shipped pre-V4 releases
V4 readiness gate is checked off or explicitly marked incomplete
V4 connectivity remains defined as external collectors later, not part of the pre-V4 releases
A final handoff summarizes what Cursor shipped and what remains
